lead: Day two of the amended S-1: an op-ed tells the SEC to block the IPO outright, Henry Blodget's arithmetic says Anthropic barely grew after July, the WSJ hears $1.5T, and the risk factors disclose an 'imminent' RSI threshold. Meanwhile Mandiant names the LLMJacking economy and Legora's CTO explains how you evaluate agents whose work you are never allowed to see.

sections.title: Reading the S-1
sections.intro: The filing gets its second, harsher day of scrutiny: Scherer wants the SEC to block the IPO over $582B in non-cancelable obligations, Blodget's monthly arithmetic shows growth flattening after July, institutional investors talk the valuation down to $1.5-1.6T - and the risk factors admit Anthropic may 'imminently' hit its own RSI threshold and has missed accelerations before.

sections.title: The legal vertical
sections.intro: Latent Space's two-part Legora conversation: $100M ARR in 18 months, two $550M rounds in seven months - and the hardest evals problem in applied AI, since client confidentiality means never reading a single trace.

sections.title: The weight-space debate
sections.intro: Sean Goedecke reads the weight-space programming paper and reaches for the cold water: a smart human with three lines of numpy could do most of it, and the honest claim is 'better than expected,' not 'superhuman.' AINews adds that an independent reproduction may already have confirmed the capability - and notes its own co-author is on the paper.

sections.title: The abuse economy
sections.intro: Mandiant and GTIG document LLMJacking: stolen API keys and identity tokens funneled through 'LLM Mixers' that resell illicit access - $100K in fraudulent charges in a day, $1M cumulative at some victims.

sections.title: The limits land
sections.intro: Developers report Opus 5.5 refusing reverse-engineering and analysis tasks beyond the confirmed game-clone limits; the workaround of record is deliberately downgrading to an older model.

sections.title: The money keeps moving
sections.intro: Trajectory raises $45M from Sequoia to automate post-training for companies without research teams; Apple posts a record $114.5B quarter with no compute story attached.

sections.title: The hardware horizon
sections.intro: Fujifilm quintuples LTO tape capacity for the AI archiving boom - the buildout's supply chain reaches back to the 1950s. WiCi bets on the opposite architecture: a wireless GPU box that serves local inference to every device in the house.

sections.title: The workbench
sections.intro: llm 0.37 lands, and Willison reports the AI-PR flood is manageable when you triage it with models - 'bug reports with attached examples.'

sections.title: The engineering shelf
sections.intro: OpenAI engineering on scaling Git for its development org; the source page was unretrievable, so details await a successful fetch.

sections.title: The lopsided boom
sections.intro: The ABC maps an S&P 500 where tech is 44% of value and the AI trade is the index's center of gravity - masking weakness elsewhere and concentrating repricing risk in every retirement account.

sections.title: The shelf life of findings
sections.intro: A mass replication re-ran 50 widely cited LLM findings across 20 models: within 15 months, 44% had expired and another 34% weakened. Behavioral claims about 'how LLMs act' are time-stamped measurements, not durable facts.

sections.title: The open-weight economics
sections.intro: Gartner's planning assumption: 90% of enterprise agent workflow steps will run on open-weight models by 2030 - routine steps at a quarter of the price, control of workflow history as the real argument, and harnesses as the layer where value concentrates.

sections.title: The politics of safety
sections.intro: NYMag profiles Alex Bores, the RAISE Act sponsor turned martyr of the $8M super-PAC hit, now launching Who Decides to make AI safety a default Democratic position for 2028.

sections.title: The consumer push
sections.intro: Google takes Dreambeans to India with 13 languages - looking for the audience the proactive-story app hasn't found in the US, where downloads fell 84% in October.

sections.title: The security desk
sections.intro: OpenAI partners with Cathedral and quadruples top bug-bounty rewards - paying up to be attacked on friendly terms, the same week an autonomous AI pentest framework shows up in a real breach notification.

sections.title: Export controls, mirrored
sections.intro: Huawei's flagship Ascend 960DT will reportedly run on Samsung and SK Hynix HBM - the porous side of the controls - while Nvidia verbally orders cloud clients to sell 51%+ of services to non-Chinese customers, policing the rental channel itself.

sections.title: The adoption question
sections.intro: Larridin raises $30M from Pelion to measure how AI actually affects employee output - the analytics layer for enterprises auditing their AI bills.
